Safety surcharge on railway fares
*421. DR. ABRAR AHMED:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the Minister of  RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether railways propose to raise
Rs. 5000 crores through levy of safety
surcharge on passenger fares towards a non-
lapsable railway safety fund over a period
of six years; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Transfer of technologies
*422. SHRI K. NATWAR SINGH:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of  HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Russia have
decided to set up a joint venture for transfer
of technologies, evolved through
collaborative efforts, to developed and
developing countries;
(b) if so, whether the two countries
have also identified new key scientific
projects, including some in strategic areas
for collaboration; if so,  details in this
regard;
(c) whether a Russian-Indian centre for
Ayurvedic Research is also underway;
(d) if so, whether this decision was
taken at a meeting he had with a 20 member
Russian delegation; and
(e) if so, what are the follow up steps
being taken in this regard?
Literacy rate among Muslim women
*423. SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM: Will
the Minister of  HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the literacy rate among
Muslim women is growing in India;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Cleaning of river water
†*424. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of  ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have as a target, fixed the year  2007 as
final time limit for making water of all the
major rivers of the country clean;

125
WIN2\SESSION\2515RS 125
(b) if so, the names of these rivers;
(c) the quantity of water available at
present for different uses in these rivers;
and
(d) the estimate with regard to
availability of additional water from these
rivers after 2007?
National Programme for Education of
Girls
*425. SHRIMATI SHABANA
AZMI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of  HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have cleared
the ambitious National Programme for
Education of Girls at the elementary level;
(b) if so, the details of the programme;
(c) what is the total amount set for this
purpose;
(d) by what time the programme is
likely to be implemented; and
(e) the States where this Programme is
likely to be introduced?
Air pollution in metros
*426. SHRI R.K. ANAND:
SHRI JHUMUK LAL
BHENDIA:
Will the Minister of  ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Centre for Science and
Environment (CSE) has recently conducted
a study about the increasing threat of air
pollution in major metros;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto;
(c) whether it is a fact that according to
CSE there are many harmful pollutants still
in the air that cause many, illnesses and
even cancer; and
(d) what further steps Government are
willing to take to reduce air pollution further
in all metros and big and small cities to
ensure the health of its citizens?
Non-availability of water at
railway stations
†*427. DR. AKHTAR HASAN RIZVI:
Will the Minister of  RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that most of the taps at railway
stations have gone dry;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps taken by Government in
this direction?
Recovery of overcharged amount
†*428. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN
SINGH 'LALAN':
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of  CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Supreme
Court has directed Government to recover
immediately 50 per cent of amount from
drug companies on account of overcharging
from consumers for the drugs;
(b) if so, the details of such drug
manufacturers and amount overcharged by
each of them from consumers; and
(c) the action taken to recover 50 per
cent of the said amount?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Foreign exchange earned by Palace
on Wheels
*429. SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH
LIBRA:
DR. ABRAR AHMED:
Will the Minister of  RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) what has been the average occupancy
of 'Palace on Wheels', the luxury train during
the year 2002-2003;
(b) the foreign exchange earned by it
during the above period; and
(c) what further steps are being taken
by Government to make the train more
popular for tourists?

Infrastructure for Agriculture
Research and Education in U.P.
†3163. DR. AKHTAR HASAN RIZVI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the basic infrastructure
provided to Uttar Pradesh for agriculture
research and education;
(b) whether the basic infrastructure
provided to the State is sufficient; and
(c) if not, the steps being taken to step
up the same?
Improving quality of groundnuts
3164. SHRI PARMESHWAR
KUMAR AGARWALLA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India
produces the maximum amount of
groundnuts in the world;
(b) if so, whether, inspite of this, India's
exports of groundnuts are negligible; and
(c) if so, what steps are being taken to
improve the quality of groundnuts in the
country?
Infrastructure for Agriculture Research
and Education in Gujarat
3165. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) what infrastructure has been
provided to Gujarat for agriculture research
and education;
(b) whether this infrastructure in that
State is inadequate;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) what steps are being taken to
augment the existing infrastructure to raise
it up to the desired level?
Suicides by farmers
3166. SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN:
SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of farmers who
have committed suicides in different parts
of the country during 1999-2000 to 2002-
2003 June end, State-wise and year-wise;
(b) the total amount of compensation
paid to the families of these unfortunate
farmers, year-wise and State-wise;

693
Win2/SESSION\2516RS 693
(c) whether Government are aware of
the main reasons for the incidences of
suicide;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) what action Government are taking
to avoid such incidents in future?
Assistance to U.P. for agricultural
projects
†3167. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of financial assistance
given by the Central Government to Uttar
Pradesh during the last two years for the
development and upgradation of agricultural
projects;
(b) whether the amount given by the
Central Government for this purpose has
been utilised completely by the State; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Financial allocation to ICAR
3168. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal to reduce
financial allocations for the ICAR;
(b) whether it is a fact that the ICAR
has not been able to contribute in a
proportionate manner to farmers and others
for the huge investments being made on an
annual basis in it;
(c) what steps will be taken to verify
the inactive and non-contributory wings or
institutes under the ICAR;
(d) whether any study has been done in
this regard; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Drought relief to States
3169. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have released 6.34 lakh tonnes of foodgrains
for July, 2003 to drought affected areas;
(b) if so, the details of allocation made,
State-wise;
(c) whether drought situation in certain
States, including Andhra Pradesh, has
improved whereas some States, like
Karnataka are still experiencing deficit
rainfall;
(d) whether notwithstanding this
realisation, higher allocation of foodgrains
has been made to States where there is
mitigation of drought, in comparison with
the States still starving for rain water; and
(e) if so, the reasons for this disparity/
discrimination in natural crisis?
Amendments in Agricultural Products
and Marketing Act
3170. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
bring a legislation for a change in the existing
age old Agricultural Products and
Marketing Act;
(b) whether the existing laws have
immensely benefited the middle-men rather
than farmers for which it was actually
framed;
(c) if so, what are the main provisions
of the Act that are being changed; and
(d) to what extent, these changes will
help farmers rather than middle-men?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it has been proposed to fix
a Minimum Support Price (MSP) for
paddy during 2003-04 at Rs. 550/-
